subject: Nanotechnology
title: The Future of DNA Nanotechnology
description: Learn The Future of DNA Nanotechnology in one minute.

hook.text: DNA nanotechnology is 40 years old — Nadrian Seeman's 1982 vision is now a global research field. What comes next?

buildup.text: Cost reduction in DNA synthesis, enzymatic production of scaffolds, and AI-assisted design are accelerating the field.

discovery.text: Clinical translation is the next frontier — DNA nanostructures must prove safe, stable, and manufacturable at scale.

twist.text: RNA origami may leapfrog DNA — it can be produced by cellular transcription, sidestepping synthetic DNA costs entirely.

climax.text: The vision: programmable molecular factories that assemble products atom by atom — DNA nanotechnology is the first step.

punchline.text: From a 1982 sketch to molecular robots — DNA nanotech is just getting started.

quiz.question: What advantage could RNA origami have over DNA origami?
options: RNA is more stable than DNA in all conditions
RNA can be produced by cellular transcription, potentially avoiding the high cost of synthetic DNA
RNA origami folds into larger structures than DNA
